user_review.method: Maintainer walk-through of the public metadata and four scoped requests, plus executed CLI tests and a replay of two private saved-source manifests. Evidence below distinguishes executed checks from simulated routing. No independent user test was run.

scenarios.request: Review what changed between two 200-record research snapshots without loading them both into the model.
scenarios.expected: Compare all records, keep the full set of changed source references, and distinguish absence from deletion.
scenarios.observed: Executed comparison recovered all 68 records across four pages: 33 additions, two metadata updates and 33 not seen. 165 matched rows were left out of the delta; both input manifests were unchanged.

scenarios.request: Compare a partial scan with conflicting copies of one record.
scenarios.expected: Stop with a diagnostic rather than selecting one revision silently.
scenarios.observed: The CLI exited 2, returned a conflicting duplicate message and emitted no success JSON. Fixture files remained unchanged.

scenarios.request: Use the Ponytail reuse check before fixing a behavior that is already implemented in a shared component.
scenarios.expected: Inspect the real entry and affected callers, reuse when compatible, and test the completed path.
scenarios.observed: Body walk-through selects the working component and its callers before proposing new code. It keeps accessibility, data and failure behavior in the acceptance boundary.

scenarios.request: Give a short answer to an ordinary one-line wording question.
scenarios.expected: Use direct work with no snapshot or measurement procedure.
scenarios.observed: The description is scoped to context costs, repeated large reads and explicit reuse checks. The body keeps small requests direct.

scenarios.request: Estimate the subscription savings from a shorter tool response.
scenarios.expected: Keep payload size, actual tokens and official subscription meter separate.
scenarios.observed: Measurement walk-through reports the bytes that were measured. It leaves actual token and subscription changes unmeasured without a completed comparable run.

similar_skills.learned: Check reuse and all affected callers before writing the smallest complete change.
similar_skills.reason: The bounded Ponytail reuse check retains acceptance and failure behavior without making all coding a session mode.

similar_skills.learned: Separate source reading, tool output and generated response or implementation costs.
similar_skills.reason: The entrypoint chooses one observed bottleneck and reuses already available tools without a fixed tool stack.

similar_skills.learned: Store bulky observations with recoverable source references and measure the effect of optimization.
similar_skills.reason: The local comparator emits scoped changes and makes partial coverage explicit. The measurement guide includes the cost of coordination and retries.

similar_skills.learned: Process complete local inputs before returning relevant evidence.
similar_skills.reason: The shipped helper compares explicit manifests from the existing task rather than adding hooks, databases or a runtime service.

similar_skills.learned: Filtered output is a separate measure and a suspicious result needs access to original output.
similar_skills.reason: The workflow keeps original failures retrievable and measures real bytes without inferring provider token or subscription savings.

similar_skills.learned: Concise output still needs exact facts and unambiguous language.
similar_skills.reason: The skill reduces repeated inputs and unnecessary code first and leaves reporting in normal language.

validation.observed: 6 CLI tests passed from isolated fixture directories, including complete paging, conflict handling, scope checks and file preservation.

Both 200-record projections were checked against an independent ID-and-field comparison. All delta rows recovered across four pages. 72,574 input bytes vs 14,852 output bytes. Metadata selection and byte measurements only.
Valid skill entrypoint after final metadata edit.
